matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: First compute the integer values of both sides (evaluating any arithmetic expression) and find the numeric imbalance. Then look for a single‑stick move that changes a numeral or operator by exactly that amount (or a combination that nets the imbalance). This focuses the search on moves that can actually fix the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever the equation is false and you have identified the numeric difference between the two sides.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick arbitrarily without checking the numeric difference, which leaves the equation still false.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and a V appears on the side that needs to increase, move one of V’s diagonal sticks to create an X, raising that numeral’s value by 5 while keeping both symbols valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the difference between sides is 5 and a V is present on the lower‑value side.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from V and discarding it, leaving an invalid numeral, instead of turning V into X.

matchstick.title: Change + to - and add I
matchstick.principle: To turn a plus sign into a minus, remove its vertical stick; then place that stick as a new I (vertical) in a numeral that can accept an extra I, thereby adjusting the arithmetic while preserving the total stick count.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance is 1 and the equation contains a plus sign that can be turned into a minus.
matchstick.example: Changing + to – but forgetting to add the removed vertical stick elsewhere, resulting in a missing stick.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: You may move a vertical I‑stick from any numeral that contains at least one I, provided the source numeral remains a valid Roman numeral after removal and the destination numeral becomes a valid numeral after addition. This works even when the source numeral originally had only a single I.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance can be fixed by decreasing one side by 1 and increasing the other side by 1, and an I‑stick is available on the side that needs to lose a unit.
matchstick.example: Removing the only I from a numeral XI and leaving just X (still valid), then adding that I to another numeral.

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If both a minus sign and an equals sign appear, you can exchange them by moving one horizontal stick from the equals sign to the minus sign, turning the minus into an equals and the equals into a minus while keeping both operators valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is false but swapping the roles of ‘-’ and ‘=’ would balance the numeric values.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from ‘=’ but forgetting to leave at least two horizontals, resulting in an invalid ‘=’.

matchstick.title: Ensure a valid '=' remains when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: The equals sign must always consist of two horizontal sticks. If you take a stick away from it, you must leave exactly one horizontal (forming a minus) and you must not leave it with zero horizontals; any relocation must preserve a valid operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you relocate a stick from the equality sign.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal from ‘=’ and discarding it, leaving a single vertical line that is not a valid operator.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and an X appears on the side that needs to decrease, remove one of X’s diagonal sticks and use it to form a V, thereby reducing the value by 5 while keeping both symbols valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the difference between sides is 5 and an X is present on the higher‑value side.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal stick from X and leaving a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Evaluate expressions when computing numeric imbalance
matchstick.principle: Before comparing the two sides, fully evaluate any arithmetic expressions (e.g., “XI + I”) to obtain their integer values; then compute the imbalance. Skipping this step can lead to mis‑balancing the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving any matchstick equation that contains ‘+’ or ‘-’ on a side.
matchstick.example: Comparing “XI + I” as the string “XI+I” without evaluating it, leading to an incorrect numeric difference.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick across equality
matchstick.principle: When the numeric imbalance is exactly 2, moving a single I‑stick from a numeral on the side with excess to a numeral on the opposite side changes both sides by 1, thereby balancing the equation. Ensure both source and destination numerals stay valid after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the difference between sides is 2 and an I‑stick is present on the higher‑value side.
matchstick.example: Moving the only I from “XI” to the left‑hand “X”, turning the equation into “XI = X + I” without checking that both resulting numerals are valid.

matchstick.title: Reposition I before X to change XI to IX
matchstick.principle: If a numeral “XI” appears, moving its I‑stick to the left of the X changes the numeral to “IX”, decreasing its value by 2 while keeping both symbols valid. This is useful when the equation is off by exactly 2.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance is 2 and the side with excess contains the pattern “XI”.
matchstick.example: Moving the I from “XI” but placing it elsewhere (e.g., on the right side), leaving “XI” unchanged and the equation still false.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V, solitary I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any stick can be removed, ignoring the structural constraints of Roman numerals.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Before removing a stick, verify that the source numeral will still be a valid Roman numeral after the removal.

matchstick.description: Providing an invalid equation after moving a stick (including incomplete or unreachable solutions)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the stick move but neglects to check the overall syntactic and semantic validity of the resulting expression.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each proposed move, re‑evaluate the entire equation for correct Roman numeral syntax and arithmetic truth.

matchstick.description: Changing – to + without adding the required vertical stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats operators as independent symbols and forgets that a plus sign requires both a horizontal and a vertical stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When converting ‘-’ to ‘+’, ensure you also supply a vertical stick, typically taken from another symbol.

matchstick.description: Using an angled stick as a vertical stick (or vice versa)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model does not keep track of stick orientation when relocating pieces.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Maintain the orientation of each stick (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) when moving it; a diagonal cannot become vertical.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from the equality sign and leaving no valid '=' sign in the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may remove a horizontal from ‘=’ without ensuring a second horizontal remains, breaking the operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: If you take a stick from ‘=’, leave exactly one horizontal to form ‘-’, or move a horizontal to another ‘=’ so that both sides retain valid operators.
